title: Character Polynomials, FI-Modules, and Representation Stability

items.title: The category FI and FI-modules over a commutative ring
items.statement: Let $FI$ be the category whose objects are the finite sets and whose morphisms are the injections ([[def-category]]); it is equivalent to the full subcategory on the objects $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, $n\ge0$, so that $\operatorname{End}_{FI}([n])\cong S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]). An **FI-module over a commutative ring $k$** ([[def-commutative-ring]]) is a covariant functor $V\colon FI\to k\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]], [[def-left-and-right-modules]]); write $V_S=V(S)$, $V_n=V([n])$ and $f_*=V(f)$ for a morphism $f$. Since $\operatorname{End}_{FI}([n])=S_n$, the maps $V_n\to V_n$ induced by permutations make $V_n$ a left $kS_n$-module ([[def-group-ring]]), and each $f_*\colon V_m\to V_n$ is equivariant for the conjugation homomorphism $S_m\to S_n$ determined by $f$. A **sub-FI-module** of $V$ is a subfunctor of $V$ ([[def-submodule]]), a **map of FI-modules** is a natural transformation, and kernels, images and cokernels are computed pointwise, so the FI-modules over $k$ inherit an abelian-category structure from $k\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-quotient-module]]). An **FB-module** over $k$ is a functor from the groupoid $FB$ of finite sets and bijections to $k\text{-Mod}$; an FB-module is determined up to isomorphism by the $kS_n$-modules $W_n$ and carries no transition maps.
items.strategy: Definition pack: spell out that the equivalence $FI\simeq\{[n]\}$ fixes the endomorphism groups as the symmetric groups, that a functor sends each injection to a $k$-linear map with $V(g\circ f)=V(g)\circ V(f)$ and $V(\mathrm{id}_S)=\mathrm{id}_{V_S}$, and that pointwise kernels and cokernels satisfy the functor axioms because $k\text{-Mod}$ is abelian. No naturality properties beyond the functor axioms are asserted; natural transformations are only named, not used here.

items.title: Span, finite generation and generation degree of an FI-module
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ and let $\Sigma\subseteq\bigsqcup_S V_S$ be a set of elements. The **sub-FI-module generated by $\Sigma$**, written $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$, is the intersection of all sub-FI-modules of $V$ containing $\Sigma$; it is the smallest such sub-FI-module and consists of all finite $k$-linear combinations of elements $f_*(v)$ with $v\in\Sigma$ and $f$ a morphism of $FI$. Call $V$ **finitely generated** when $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)=V$ for some finite $\Sigma$, and **generated in degree $\le d$** when $\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le d})=V$, where $V_{\le d}=\bigsqcup_{|S|\le d}V_S$; the **generation degree** is the least such $d$, and $\infty$ when no such $d$ exists ([[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]]). Finite generation of $V$ and pointwise finite generation of the $k$-modules $V_S$ are different conditions: the latter is implied by the former ([[lem-generated-in-degree-d-is-a-quotient-of-free-fi-modules]]) but does not imply it, and no pointwise finite-dimensionality is built into either notion ([[def-submodule]] for the span).
items.strategy: Define the intersection as in the generated-submodule construction, verify it is a subfunctor and that it is exactly the set of finite combinations of images of generators (the finite-combination set is itself a subfunctor containing $\Sigma$), and record that a degree bound on generators is an additional structure, not a consequence of finite generation. Separate the two finite-generation notions in prose; no arithmetic claim is made here.

items.title: The coinvariant functors $\Phi_a$ and the transition maps $T$
items.statement: A **graded $k[T]$-module** consists of $k$-modules $U_n$, $n\ge0$, together with $k$-linear maps $T\colon U_n\to U_{n+1}$ for all $n$. Fix $a\ge0$, a set $\mathbf a$ of cardinality $a$ and a functorial disjoint union. For an FI-module $V$ over $k$ and $n\ge0$ put $$\Phi_a(V)_n:=(V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n})_{S_n},$$ the coinvariants of the $kS_n$-module $V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$ ([[def-coinvariants-functor-of-a-group-module]], [[def-quotient-module]]). Any injection $f\colon n\to n+1$ gives an injection $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup f\colon\mathbf a\sqcup n\to\mathbf a\sqcup n+1$ and an induced map $\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$; postcomposition by $S_{n+1}$ shows that this map depends only on $f$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}$, because any two injections $n\to n+1$ differ by an element of $S_{n+1}$. Writing $T$ for it, $(\Phi_a(V),T)$ is a graded $k[T]$-module, and $\Phi_a$ is a functor from FI-modules to graded $k[T]$-modules. Each $\Phi_a$ is right exact in every degree, and is exact when $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$, since averaging over the finite groups $S_n$ splits the coinvariant quotient; in that case $\Phi_a(W)\subseteq\Phi_a(V)$ for every sub-FI-module $W\subseteq V$.
items.strategy: Choice-independence of $T$: the two injections differ by a permutation of $n+1$, and coinvariants identify the images. Functoriality and right exactness are pointwise from the right-exact coinvariant functor; left exactness over a $\mathbb Q$-algebra follows because $(V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n})_{S_n}\to V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$ is split by the averaging map $v\mapsto\frac1{n!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\sigma v$, which is defined when $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$ and is natural ([[def-coinvariants-functor-of-a-group-module]], [[def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel]]).

items.title: Injectivity, surjectivity and stability degree
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$. The **injectivity degree** $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)$ (respectively the **surjectivity degree** $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)$) is the least $s\ge0$ such that for every $a\ge0$ the transition map $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is injective (respectively surjective) for all $n\ge s$; the **stability degree** is $$\operatorname{stab-deg}(V):=\max\bigl(\operatorname{inj-deg}(V),\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\bigr).$$ Each of the three is $+\infty$ when no such $s$ exists. Equivalently, $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is an isomorphism for all $a\ge0$ and all $n\ge\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)$. The three bounds are kept distinct: stability degree is the max, and injectivity and surjectivity degree need not agree in examples.
items.strategy: Unwrap the definitions ($\max$ of two extended nonnegative integers), and record the equivalent indexing statement as a reformulation: $T$ is an isomorphism iff it is both injective and surjective, and each of the two stated bounds is the least threshold controlling the corresponding property. No claim of finiteness is made; $\infty$ is allowed throughout.

items.title: Specht modules classify the irreducibles over every field of characteristic zero
items.statement: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $n\ge0$. The field-valued Specht modules $S^\lambda_F$, $\lambda\vdash n$, of [[def-polytabloid-specht-module-over-an-arbitrary-field]] are nonzero, irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic, and every irreducible $F S_n$-module is isomorphic to exactly one of them; consequently, by Maschke, every finite-dimensional $F S_n$-module is a direct sum of copies of the $S^\lambda_F$, so the irreducible $F S_n$-modules are indexed by the partitions of $n$ and the $S^\lambda_F$ form a complete irredundant list. This is the constituent convention used throughout the pair: over $F=\mathbb C$ it specialises to the published complex classification, and over a general characteristic-zero field it is transported from it by scalar extension, not assumed.
items.strategy:
(1) Base change. For every field extension $E/F$ there is an isomorphism $E\otimes_FS^\lambda_F\cong S^\lambda_E$: the canonical map $E\otimes_FM^\lambda_F	o M^\lambda_E$ is an isomorphism of $E S_n$-modules because the tabloids form the same basis after extension, and it carries the span of the polytabloids onto the span of the polytabloids ([[def-polytabloid-specht-module-over-an-arbitrary-field]], [[def-restriction-and-extension-of-scalars]], [[thm-tensor-products-commute-with-arbitrary-direct-sums]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]); surjectivity is clear and both $E$-spaces have dimension $f^\lambda$ by the field-uniform standard basis ([[lem-integral-specht-garnir-straightening-and-field-basis]]), so it is an isomorphism. In particular $\mathbb C\otimes_FS^\lambda_F\cong S^\lambda_{\mathbb C}$ and $\dim_FS^\lambda_F=f^\lambda>0$ for every $F$. (2) Irreducibility over $F$. If $S^\lambda_F=U\oplus U'$ with $U
eq0$ and $U'
eq0$, then applying the exact functor $\mathbb C\otimes_F(-)$ gives a decomposition of $S^\lambda_{\mathbb C}$ into two nonzero submodules, because $\mathbb C\otimes_FU$ and $\mathbb C\otimes_FU'$ are nonzero $\mathbb C$-vector spaces; this contradicts [[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]]. (3) Pairwise inequivalence. An $F S_n$-isomorphism $S^\lambda_F\cong S^\mu_F$ becomes a $\mathbb C S_n$-isomorphism $S^\lambda_{\mathbb C}\cong S^\mu_{\mathbb C}$, so $\lambda=\mu$ by [[cor-distinct-specht-modules-are-inequivalent]]. (4) Completeness. Let $W$ be an irreducible $F S_n$-module; it is finite-dimensional, being a quotient of the regular module $F S_n$ via $a\mapsto aw$ for a fixed $w
eq0$. Then $\mathbb C\otimes_FW$ is a nonzero $\mathbb C S_n$-module, so by the complex classification it has an irreducible constituent $S^\lambda_{\mathbb C}$ ([[thm-complex-irreducibles-of-symmetric-groups-are-specht-modules]]). For finite-dimensional $V$ the natural map $\mathbb C\otimes_F\operatorname{Hom}_F(V,W)	o\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb C\otimes_FV,\mathbb C\otimes_FW)$, $c\otimes f\mapsto(c'\otimes v\mapsto cc'\otimes f(v))$, is a $\mathbb C$-linear isomorphism and restricts to an isomorphism of the $G$-equivariant maps; hence $\operatorname{Hom}_{FS_n}(S^\lambda_F,W)
eq0$, and since both modules are irreducible over $F$ (step 2) $W\cong S^\lambda_F$. Finally Maschke ([[thm-maschkes-theorem-for-finite-groups-over-fields-whose-characteristic-does-not-divide-the-group-order]]) splits every finite-dimensional $F S_n$-module into irreducibles, which by this argument are the $S^\lambda_F$. No choice principle is used: the field extensions and finite-dimensional linear algebra are explicit.

items.title: Weight of an FI-module over a field of characteristic zero
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). For a partition $\lambda$ and $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ put $\lambda[n]:=(n-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$, the first-row padding ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), and let $V(\lambda)_n$ denote the irreducible $kS_n$-module indexed by the partition $\lambda[n]$, i.e. the scalar extension to $k$ of the complex Specht module $S^{\lambda[n]}$ ([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]], [[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]). The **weight** of $V$ is $$\operatorname{weight}(V):=\sup\{|\lambda|:V(\lambda)_n\text{ occurs as a constituent of }V_n\text{ for some }n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1\},$$ the supremum over all pairs $(\lambda,n)$ as displayed; it is $0$ for $V=0$ and $+\infty$ when the set is unbounded. If $W$ is a subquotient of $V$ then $\operatorname{weight}(W)\le\operatorname{weight}(V)$.
items.strategy: Well-definedness: every partition of $n$ is uniquely $\lambda[n]$ for a partition $\lambda$ (the boxes below the first row form a partition), so the constituent labels are well defined and the supremum is over a set of nonnegative integers. The subquotient inequality is immediate since constituents of a subquotient are constituents of $V$. The item records the convention that $k$ may be any characteristic-zero field via the absolute irreducibility supplied by the classification lemma; no finiteness of $\operatorname{weight}(V)$ is asserted.

items.title: The free FI-module $M(W)$ generated by an $S_m$-module
items.statement: Let $W$ be an FB-module over $k$, i.e. a family of $kS_m$-modules $W_m$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). The **free FI-module** $M(W)$ is the FI-module with $$M(W)_S:=\bigoplus_{T\subseteq S}W_T,$$ where $W_T$ denotes $W_{|T|}$ transported along a bijection $T\to[|T|]$ (well defined up to canonical isomorphism), and on an injection $f\colon S\to S'$ the map $M(W)_S\to M(W)_{S'}$ is the sum of the maps $W_T\to W_{f(T)}$ induced by $f|_T$ ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). $M(-)$ is the left adjoint of the forgetful functor from FI-modules to FB-modules, so $$\operatorname{Hom}_{FI\text{-}Mod}(M(W),V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{FB\text{-}Mod}(W,\pi V)$$ naturally in $V$; the unit sends $W_S$ to the summand $W_S$ of $M(W)_S$. As an $S_n$-module, $$M(W)_n\cong\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n}\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_{n-a}}^{S_n}\bigl(W_a\boxtimes k\bigr),$$ with $\boxtimes$ the external tensor product of modules for the direct factors and $\operatorname{Ind}$ the induced module built from $H$-covariant functions ([[def-induced-r-linear-g-module-by-h-covariant-functions]], [[def-outer-induction-product-for-symmetric-group-characters]], [[lem-character-ring-of-a-direct-product-is-the-tensor-product]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]). For $m\ge0$, $M(m):=M(k[S_m])$ has as a $k$-basis the injections $m\to S$; for a partition $\lambda$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $0$, $M(\lambda):=M(S^\lambda_k)$.
items.strategy: Existence and functoriality of $M(W)$: the summands $W_T$ depend on $T$ only up to the canonical transport along the unique bijection between two $|T|$-element sets, and $f$ sends $T$ to $f(T)$, giving compatible maps; the adjunction is checked on the unit and co-unit (evaluate at $S=\emptyset$ and at singletons). The $S_n$-module identification is the orbit decomposition of the sum over subsets, each orbit contributing $\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_{n-a}}^{S_n}(W_a\boxtimes k)$. No choice beyond finite transport data is used.

items.title: Generation in bounded degree presents an FI-module as a quotient of free FI-modules
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$. (a) For $v\in V_m$ the FI-module map $M(m)\to V$ sending the basis element $\mathrm{id}_m\in M(m)_m$ to $v$ has image $\operatorname{span}_V(v)$; more generally, for any $\Sigma\subseteq\bigsqcup_S V_S$ the canonical map $\bigoplus_{s\in\Sigma}M(|S_s|)\to V$ has image $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$. (b) $V$ is finitely generated if and only if there is a finite family $m_1,\dots,m_k\ge0$ with a surjection $M(m_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus M(m_k)\twoheadrightarrow V$; $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$ if and only if there is a surjection $\bigoplus_{i\in I}M(m_i)\twoheadrightarrow V$ with $m_i\le d$ for all $i$. In particular, if $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$ then the evaluation map $\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)\to V$ is surjective, where $V_m$ is regarded as an FB-module. (c) If $V$ is finitely generated, then $V_S$ is a finitely generated $k$-module for every finite set $S$.
items.strategy: For (a), the image of $M(m)\to V$ is spanned by the elements $f_*(v)$, and every sub-FI-module containing $v$ contains these elements; the general $\Sigma$ case is the same computation on a direct sum. For (b), a finite generating set defines a map from a finite sum of free modules by (a), which is surjective by definition of generation; conversely the images of the canonical generators $\mathrm{id}_{m_i}\in M(m_i)_{m_i}$ generate the image ([[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]]). Taking the generating set $V_{\le d}$ gives the evaluation map. For (c), a surjection $\bigoplus_i M(m_i)\twoheadrightarrow V$ restricts at $S$ to a surjection of $k$-modules onto $V_S$ from a finite direct sum of free $k$-modules, which is a finitely generated $k$-module.

items.title: Branching rule for Specht modules: adding or removing boxes in distinct columns
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $\lambda\vdash n$ and let $S^\lambda_F$ be the corresponding Specht module. (i) For every $k\ge0$ there is an isomorphism of $F S_{n+k}$-modules $$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_n	imes S_k}^{S_{n+k}} igl(S^\lambda_F oxtimes F igr)\cong igoplus_{\mu}S^\mu_F,$$ summed over the partitions $\mu\vdash n+k$ obtained from $\lambda$ by adding one box to each of $k$ different columns. (ii) For every $k\le n$ there is an isomorphism of $F S_{n-k}$-modules $$ igl(\operatorname{Res}^{S_n}_{S_{n-k}	imes S_k}S^\lambda_F igr)_{S_k}\cong igoplus_{
u}S^
u_F,$$ summed over the partitions $
u\vdash n-k$ obtained from $\lambda$ by removing one box from each of $k$ different columns. All multiplicities are $0$ or $1$.

Part (i) is the outer Pieri rule with trivial factors ([[cor-outer-pieri-rules-for-trivial-and-sign-factors]]) read off in the Specht basis supplied by [[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]. For (ii), Frobenius reciprocity for complex characters ([[cor-frobenius-reciprocity-for-complex-characters]]) identifies the multiplicity of $S^
u_F$ in the $S_k$-coinvariants of the restriction with the multiplicity of $S^\lambda_F$ in $\operatorname{Ind}_{S_{n-k}	imes S_k}^{S_{n-k}}(S^
u_F oxtimes F)$, which is $1$ exactly when $\lambda/
u$ is a horizontal $k$-strip by (i); the coinvariant quotient is semisimple over $F$ of characteristic $0$ by Maschke, so multiplicities determine the module. No other summands occur because (i) lists exactly the horizontal-strip shapes.

items.title: Free FI-modules have computable stability degree and weight
items.statement: Let $W$ be an FB-module over $k$. Then $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(W))=0$, and if $W_i=0$ for $i>m$ then $\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(W))\le m$; in particular $M(m)=M(k[S_m])$ has $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(m))=0$ and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(m))=m$. If moreover $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $\lambda$ is a partition, then $\operatorname{weight}(M(\lambda))=|\lambda|$ and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(\lambda))=\lambda_1$.
items.strategy: The displayed computation of $\Phi_aM(W)$ as $\bigoplus_{U\subseteq\mathbf a,0\le j\le n}\Phi_{|U|}(W)_j$ shows that $T$ preserves the summands and acts as the identity on each, giving injectivity degree $0$; when $W$ vanishes above $m$ the $j$-range is exhausted for $n\ge m$, giving surjectivity degree $\le m$, and $\Phi_0(k[S_m])_m\cong k$ gives the exact value $m$ for $M(m)$. For $M(\lambda)$, the $O_{S_n}$-constituents of $M(\lambda)_n=\operatorname{Ind}_{S_m\times S_{n-m}}^{S_n}(S^\lambda\boxtimes k)$ are described by the branching lemma (i), so a constituent $V(\mu)_n$ has $|\mu|\le|\lambda|$ with equality attained for $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$, giving weight $|\lambda|$; and part (ii) of the same lemma gives $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}\cong\operatorname{Ind}_{S_{|\lambda|}\times S_{a-|\lambda|}}^{S_a}V_\lambda\neq0$ exactly for $a\ge|\lambda|$ and $n\ge a+\lambda_1$, which is precisely the statement that $\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(\lambda))=\lambda_1$.

items.title: Bounded generation degree bounds surjectivity degree and weight
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$. (a) Every quotient $V\twoheadrightarrow W$ satisfies $\operatorname{surj-deg}(W)\le\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)$. (b) If $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$, then $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le d$. (c) If moreover $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$, then $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le d$.
items.strategy: (a) $\Phi_a$ is right exact, so $\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(W)_n$ is surjective in every degree and a surjective $T$ remains surjective on the quotient. (b) By the presentation lemma $V$ is a quotient of $\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)$, and each summand is an $M(W)$ with $W$ supported in degrees $\le d$, so it has surjectivity degree $\le d$; a finite direct sum has surjectivity degree the maximum, and (a) passes the bound to the quotient $V$. (c) The same presentation exhibits $V$ as a quotient of $\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)$, each $M(V_m)$ has weight $\le m\le d$ by the free-module bound, and weight is monotone under subquotients, so $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le d$.

items.title: Tensor products of finitely generated FI-modules are finitely generated
items.statement: Let $V$ and $W$ be finitely generated FI-modules over $k$, with pointwise tensor product $(V\otimes W)_S=V_S\otimes_k W_S$. Then $V\otimes W$ is finitely generated. More precisely, if $V$ is generated in degree $\le m_1$ and $W$ in degree $\le m_2$, then $V\otimes W$ is generated in degree $\le m_1+m_2$.
items.strategy: By the presentation lemma it suffices to treat $U=M(m_1)\otimes M(m_2)$: a $k$-basis of $U_S$ is given by pairs $(f_1\colon m_1\to S, f_2\colon m_2\to S)$, and each basis element lies in the image of $U_T$ for $T=\mathrm{im}(f_1)\cup\mathrm{im}(f_2)$ with $|T|\le m_1+m_2$; hence $U$ is generated in degree $\le m_1+m_2$. For general $V,W$ choose surjections $\bigoplus_i M(m_i)\twoheadrightarrow V$ and $\bigoplus_j M(n_j)\twoheadrightarrow W$ with all $m_i\le m_1$, $n_j\le m_2$; tensor products preserve surjections and distribute over finite direct sums ([[thm-right-exactness-of-tensor-products]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]), so $V\otimes W$ is a quotient of a finite sum of $M(m_i)\otimes M(n_j)$, each generated in degree $\le m_i+n_j\le m_1+m_2$; quotients do not increase generation degree.

items.title: Coinvariants detect vanishing of subquotients of bounded weight, and padded irreducibles stabilise
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $\mu\vdash n$ and write $\mu=\lambda[n]$ as in the padding definition. (i) For $a\le n$, with $k_0:=n-a$, the $S_a$-representation $(V_\mu)_{S_{k_0}}$ is zero if and only if $n-a>\mu_1$, equivalently $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}=0$ if and only if $a<|\lambda|$. (ii) If $n-a=\mu_1$ (that is, $a=|\lambda|$), then $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}\cong V_\lambda$ as $S_{|\lambda|}$-modules. (iii) For fixed $\lambda$ and $a\ge|\lambda|$, the $S_a$-module $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}$ is independent of $n$ once $n\ge a+\lambda_1$; in fact $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}\cong\operatorname{Ind}_{S_{|\lambda|}\times S_{a-|\lambda|}}^{S_a}(V_\lambda\boxtimes k)$ throughout that range. (iv) If $V$ is an FI-module over $k$ with $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le a$, then every subquotient $W_n$ of the $S_n$-module $V_n$ satisfies $W_n=0\iff(W_n)_{S_{n-a}}=0$.
items.strategy:
Apply the branching lemma part (ii) with $S^\lambda_F = V_\mu$: $(V_\mu)_{S_{n-a}}$ is the sum of the irreducibles $V_
u$ over partitions $
u\vdash a$ obtained from $\mu$ by removing one box from each of $n-a$ different columns; such a removal is possible iff $n-a\le\mu_1$, and when $n-a=\mu_1$ it is possible only by removing every column's bottom box, leaving $\lambda$; this gives (i) and (ii). For (iii), the removal description shows that the set of resulting $
u$ depends on $n$ only through the first row of $\mu$, and once $n\ge a+\lambda_1$ the removable columns are exactly the first $\lambda_1+(a-|\lambda|)$ columns, which yields the displayed induction independent of $n$. For (iv), decompose $W_n$ into padded irreducibles $V(\lambda)_n$; every constituent has $|\lambda|\le a$ by definition of weight, so (i) gives a nontrivial coinvariant quotient exactly when $|\lambda|\le a$, hence $W_n=0$ iff $(W_n)_{S_{n-a}}=0$.

items.title: A stability degree bounds the first row of every constituent
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$, with $s:=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)<\infty$. Then for every $n\ge0$ every irreducible constituent $V(\lambda)_n$ of the $S_n$-module $V_n$ satisfies $\lambda_1\le s$; equivalently, no constituent has first row longer than the stability degree.
items.strategy: Filter $V$ by $F^mV:=\operatorname{span}(V_{\le m})$, so that $V=\bigcup_mF^mV$ and each $F^mV$ is generated in degree $\le m$. It suffices to prove the bound for every constituent of every quotient $F^mV/F^{m-1}V$. Fix $m$ and let $\overline V:=V/F^{m-1}V$; then $\overline V_n=0$ for $n<m$ and $\overline V_m\cong H_m:=\operatorname{span}(V_{\le m})/\operatorname{span}(V_{<m})$ is its degree-$m$ part. If $m\le s+1$ then any $\mu\vdash m$ has $\mu_1\le m\le s$, so assume $m>s+1$: since $\overline V$ is a quotient of $V$, part (a) of the generation lemma gives $\operatorname{surj-deg}(\overline V)\le s$, so $T\colon\Phi_{m-s-1}(\overline V)_s\to\Phi_{m-s-1}(\overline V)_{s+1}$ is surjective; its domain is a quotient of $\overline V_{m-1}=0$, hence $0$; but $\Phi_{m-s-1}(\overline V)_{s+1}=(\overline V_m)_{S_{s+1}}$, so $(H_m)_{S_{s+1}}=0$, and the coinvariant lemma (i) with $a=s+1$ gives $\mu_1\le s$ for every constituent $V_\mu$ of $H_m$. Next, $F^mV/F^{m-1}V$ is generated in degree $\le m$ with vanishing values below $m$, so the presentation lemma gives a surjection $M(H_m)\twoheadrightarrow F^mV/F^{m-1}V$; by the free-module description every constituent of $M(H_m)_n$ is obtained from a constituent $H_\mu$ of $H_m$ by adding boxes in different columns, which cannot increase the first row beyond $\mu_1\le s$; a quotient of $M(H_m)_n$ has no other constituents. Passing along the filtration gives the claim for $V_n$.

items.title: FI-modules over a Noetherian $\mathbb Q$-algebra form a Noetherian category
items.statement: Let $k$ be a commutative Noetherian ring containing $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-noetherian-ring]]), and let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$ ([[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]]). Then every sub-FI-module $W\subseteq V$ is finitely generated; that is, the category of FI-modules over $k$ is Noetherian. The hypothesis that $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$ is used only through the exactness of the functors $\Phi_a$ and through restriction of scalars to $\mathbb Q$.
items.strategy: Let $V$ be generated in degree $\le a$ and let $W\subseteq V$. First, $V_n$ is a finitely generated $k$-module for every $n$ (presentation lemma (c)), and the graded $k[T]$-module $\Phi_a(V)$ is finitely generated: $T$ is surjective in degrees $\ge a$ by the generation-degree bound (b), so $\Phi_a(V)$ is generated over $k[T]$ by the finitely many components $\Phi_a(V)_0,\dots,\Phi_a(V)_{a-1}$, each a finitely generated $k$-module as a quotient of some $V_i$. Since $k[T]$ is Noetherian ([[thm-hilbert-basis-theorem]], [[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and a finitely generated module over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian ([[thm-finitely-generated-modules-over-noetherian-rings-are-noetherian]], [[def-noetherian-module]]), the submodule $\Phi_a(W)\subseteq\Phi_a(V)$ is a finitely generated graded $k[T]$-module; choose homogeneous generators $x_1,\dots,x_r$, lift each $x_i\in\Phi_a(W)_{n_i}$ to $w_i\in W_{a+n_i}$, and let $\widetilde W\subseteq W$ be generated by the $w_i$ together with finite generating sets of $W_0,\dots,W_{a-1}$. Then $\Phi_a(\widetilde W)=\Phi_a(W)$, and exactness of $\Phi_a$ over $\mathbb Q$-algebras gives $\Phi_a(W/\widetilde W)=0$. It remains to show $W/\widetilde W=0$, and this is done over the complex numbers, where the weight theory is carried by the published classification: base change from $k$ to $\mathbb C$ along $\mathbb Q\subseteq k\subseteq\mathbb C$ ([[def-restriction-and-extension-of-scalars]]) gives the $\mathbb C$-FI-module $U_{\mathbb C}:=\mathbb C\otimes_{\mathbb Q}U$ for any $k$-FI-module $U$, with $(W/\widetilde W)_{\mathbb C}$ a subquotient of $V_{\mathbb C}$. The $k$-module $V$ generated in degree $\le a$ has $V_{\mathbb C}$ generated in degree $\le a$ (base change is right exact), so $\operatorname{weight}(V_{\mathbb C})\le a$ over $\mathbb C$ by the generation-degree bound (c); hence every irreducible constituent $V(\lambda)_n^{\mathbb C}$ of $(W/\widetilde W)_{\mathbb C,n}$ has $|\lambda|\le a$ by monotonicity of weight. Base change commutes with coinvariants, so $\Phi_a((W/\widetilde W)_{\mathbb C})=0$; for $n\ge a$, the coinvariant lemma (i) over $\mathbb C$ gives $\bigl(V(\lambda)_n^{\mathbb C}\bigr)_{S_{n-a}}\neq0$ for every $|\lambda|\le a$, and therefore every multiplicity of such a constituent in $(W/\widetilde W)_{\mathbb C,n}$ vanishes; thus $(W/\widetilde W)_{\mathbb C,n}=0$ for $n\ge a$, hence $(W/\widetilde W)_n=0$ because base change along $\mathbb Q\to\mathbb C$ reflects zero (a nonzero vector space stays nonzero after extending scalars). For $n<a$, $\widetilde W_n=W_n$ by construction. Hence $W=\widetilde W$ is finitely generated.

items.title: Uniform representation stability for consistent sequences of $S_n$-modules
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$. A **consistent sequence** is a sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)_{n\ge0}$ in which $V_n$ is a finite-dimensional $kS_n$-module and $\varphi_n\colon V_n\to V_{n+1}$ is $S_n$-equivariant, $V_{n+1}$ being regarded as an $S_n$-module by restriction along the standard inclusion $S_n\hookrightarrow S_{n+1}$; an FI-module $V$ with finite-dimensional values determines the consistent sequence $(V_n,f_*)$ for the standard inclusions. The sequence is **uniformly representation stable with stable range $n\ge N$** when (I) $\varphi_n$ is injective for all $n\ge N$; (II) the $S_{n+1}$-span of $\varphi_n(V_n)$ is all of $V_{n+1}$ for all $n\ge N$; and (III) writing $V_n\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda}c_{\lambda,n}V(\lambda)_n$ with padded irreducibles $V(\lambda)_n$ ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), the multiplicity $c_{\lambda,n}$ is independent of $n$ for every fixed $\lambda$ and all $n\ge N$. The sequence is uniformly representation stable when it is so for some $N$. All three conditions are part of the definition; (II) is not implied by (I) and (III).
items.strategy: State the three clauses and the padding convention used in (III), and verify that an FI-module's standard-inclusion maps $f_*$ are $S_n$-equivariant by functoriality and the conjugation action. Record the known non-example (the consistent sequence of regular representations is not uniformly stable, and indeed does not come from an FI-module) only as a warning that consistency alone is weaker; no claim of it is needed here.

items.title: Weight and stability degree give a uniform representation-stability range
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values, weight $d=\operatorname{weight}(V)$ and stability degree $s=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)$. Then the consistent sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)$ is uniformly representation stable with stable range $n\ge d+s$.
items.strategy: Set $K_n=\ker\varphi_n\subseteq V_n$ and let $C_{n+1}$ be the cokernel of the $S_{n+1}$-map $\operatorname{Ind}^{S_{n+1}}_{S_n}\varphi_n\colon\operatorname{Ind}^{S_{n+1}}_{S_n}V_n\to V_{n+1}$; conditions (I) and (II) are exactly $K_n=0$ and $C_{n+1}=0$. Since $K_n$ is a subrepresentation of $V_n$ and $C_{n+1}$ a quotient of $V_{n+1}$, the coinvariant lemma (iv) reduces both to the vanishing of $(K_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ and $(C_{n+1})_{S_{n+1-d}}$ for $n\ge d$. Exactness of $S_a$-coinvariants in characteristic $0$ identifies $(K_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ with the kernel of $(\varphi_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ and $(C_{n+1})_{S_{n+1-d}}$ with the cokernel of $(\operatorname{Ind}\varphi_n)_{S_{n+1-d}}$, and the transition map $T\colon\Phi_d(V)_{n-d}\to\Phi_d(V)_{n+1-d}$ factors through both, so it is the composite in the two ways displayed in the source. For $n-d\ge s$, $T$ is an isomorphism, so $(\varphi_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ is injective and $(\operatorname{Ind}\varphi_n)_{S_{n+1-d}}$ is surjective; hence $K_n=0$ and $C_{n+1}=0$ for $n\ge s+d$. For (III), fix $m\le d$ and induct on $m=|\lambda|$: in the range $n\ge s+d$, decompose $(V_n)_{S_{n-m}}$ into constituents and use the coinvariant lemma (i) to see that only $|\lambda|\le m$ contribute, (iii) to see that the contributions of $|\lambda|<m$ are independent of $n$, and the induction hypothesis to see that their multiplicities are constant; the remaining summand is a direct sum of $\lambda$'s of size $m$ with multiplicity $c_{\lambda,n}$ by (ii), so constancy of the total forces constancy of each $c_{\lambda,n}$. Here the range hypothesis enters twice: $\lambda_1\le s$ for every occurring constituent by the first-row bound, so $n\ge s+d\ge\lambda_1+m$ puts all constituents in the range where the coinvariant lemma applies, and the isomorphism statement of the stability degree applies at $n-m\ge s$.

items.title: Finite generation is equivalent to uniform representation stability
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values. Then $V$ is finitely generated if and only if the consistent sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)$ is uniformly representation stable.
items.strategy: ($\Rightarrow$) If $V$ is generated in degree $\le g$, then $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le g$ by the generation-degree lemma (b), and the presentation lemma gives a surjection $M:=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{g}M(i)^{\oplus b_i}\twoheadrightarrow V$ with kernel $K$; by the Noetherian theorem $K$ is finitely generated, say in degree $\le r$. Exactness of $\Phi_a$ over $\mathbb Q$ writes $\Phi_a(V)\cong\Phi_a(M)/\Phi_a(K)$; the free summands have injectivity degree $0$ and $\operatorname{surj-deg}(K)\le r$, so $T$ is injective on $\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ for $n\ge r$; hence $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)\le r$, $\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)\le\max(g,r)$ and the weight is finite. The preceding proposition then gives uniform representation stability in degrees $\ge\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)+\operatorname{weight}(V)$. ($\Leftarrow$) If the sequence is uniformly representation stable for $n\ge N$, then for $n\ge N$ the $S_{n+1}$-span of $\varphi_n(V_n)$ is all of $V_{n+1}$, so the images of the finitely many $F I$-maps $V_n\to V_{n+1}$ span $V_{n+1}$; by induction $V=\operatorname{span}(V_{\le N})$, and since each $V_{\le N}$ is finite-dimensional by hypothesis, $V$ is finitely generated.

items.title: Character polynomials in the cycle counts $X_i$
items.statement: For $i\ge1$ and $n\ge0$ let $X_i\colon S_n\to\mathbb N$ be the class function sending a permutation to the number of its $i$-cycles ([[def-permutation-support-disjoint-cycles-and-cycle-type]]); thus $X_1(\sigma)$ is the number of fixed points. A **character polynomial** is a polynomial $P\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ in finitely many of the variables $X_i$, its **weighted degree** being defined by $\deg X_i:=i$ ([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Since the class functions on $S_n$ form a $\mathbb Q$-algebra under pointwise multiplication ([[def-class-function-and-the-space-of-complex-class-functions]]), every character polynomial $P$ defines a class function $P\colon S_n\to\mathbb Q$ for every $n\ge0$. The expression is not unique on a single $S_n$, since $X_i$ vanishes identically for $i>n$; it is unique in the limit: if $P$ and $Q$ agree as functions on $S_n$ for infinitely many $n$, then $P=Q$. A sequence $(\chi_n)$ of class functions with $\chi_n$ a class function on $S_n$ is **eventually polynomial** when there are $N$ and a character polynomial $P$ with $\chi_n(\sigma)=P(\sigma)$ for all $n\ge N$ and all $\sigma\in S_n$.
items.strategy: Define the $X_i$ as class functions (they are constant on conjugacy classes because cycle type is a conjugacy invariant), define evaluation and weighted degree, and prove uniqueness by evaluating at permutations that fix all but a fixed finite set: for a monomial of top weighted degree $\le M$, the substitutions $X_1\mapsto n-c$, $X_r\mapsto X_r(\rho)$ for $r\ge2$ produce a polynomial in $n$; vanishing for infinitely many $n$ forces the coefficient of the top $X_1$-power to vanish on all fixed-point-free cycle types, and descending on the $X_1$-degree gives $P=0$. No representation theory is used in this definition.

items.title: Padded irreducible characters are eventually given by character polynomials
items.statement: For every partition $\lambda$ there is a character polynomial $P_\lambda\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ of weighted degree at most $|\lambda|$ such that for every $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ and every $\sigma\in S_n$ $$\chi^{\lambda[n]}(\sigma)=P_\lambda(X_1(\sigma),X_2(\sigma),\dots),$$ where $\chi^{\lambda[n]}$ is the character of the irreducible Specht module $S^{\lambda[n]}$.
items.strategy: Classical route of Macdonald's Example I.7.14. Fix $\lambda\vdash m$ and write $N:=n-m\ge\lambda_1$. By the published character-value formula ([[cor-irreducible-symmetric-group-character-values-are-power-sum-coefficients]]) $\chi^{\lambda[n]}(\sigma)=\langle s_{\lambda[n]},p_{\rho(\sigma)}\rangle$, and the Frobenius coefficient formula applied with the $n+1$ variables $x_0,x_1,\dots,x_n$ exhibits the value as a coefficient in $\Delta\prod_rp_r^{X_r(\sigma)}$; the product is homogeneous, so the $x_0$-exponent is forced by the other exponents and the substitution $x_0=1$ removes $N$ from the extraction: $\chi^{\lambda[n]}(\sigma)=\langle E\cdot P(\sigma),s_\lambda\rangle$ with $E=\prod_i(1-x_i)$ and $P(\sigma)=\prod_{r\ge1}(1+p_r)^{X_r(\sigma)}$ in the completed stable ring, the inner product being the Hall form ([[def-hall-inner-product-on-symmetric-functions]], [[def-stable-schur-function-by-bialternants]], [[def-power-sum-and-complete-homogeneous-symmetric-polynomials]]). Since $s_\lambda$ has degree $m$, only the total-degree-$m$ component of $E\cdot P(\sigma)$ contributes; expanding $E=\sum_j(-1)^je_j$ and $P(\sigma)=\prod_r\sum_{k_r}\binom{X_r(\sigma)}{k_r}p_r^{k_r}$ shows that this component is a finite $\mathbb Q$-linear combination of products $e_jp_{r_1}^{k_1}\cdots p_{r_s}^{k_s}$ with $j+\sum r_ik_i=m$, and the Hall inner product with $s_\lambda$ of each such product is a rational constant; hence $\chi^{\lambda[n]}(\sigma)=\sum_{j+\sum r_ik_i=m}c_{j,k}s_{\lambda}\prod_r\binom{X_r(\sigma)}{k_r}$, a polynomial in the cycle counts of weighted degree $\le m$, independent of $N$. Uniqueness of the polynomial is the injectivity of the cycle-count evaluation for infinitely many $n$ recorded in the definition.

items.title: Finitely generated FI-modules have eventual character polynomials
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values, weight $d=\operatorname{weight}(V)$ and stability degree $s=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)$. Then there is a unique character polynomial $P_V\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ of weighted degree at most $d$ such that $$\chi_{V_n}(\sigma)=P_V(X_1(\sigma),X_2(\sigma),\dots)$$ for every $n\ge s+d$ and every $\sigma\in S_n$; here $\chi_{V_n}$ is the character of the $kS_n$-module $V_n$, and $\mathbb Q\subseteq k$ is the prime field.
items.strategy: By the stability-range proposition applied to $V$, there are constants $c_\lambda\ge0$ with $V_n\cong\bigoplus_\lambda c_\lambda V(\lambda)_n$ for all $n\ge s+d$, the sum over the finitely many $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|\le d$. For each such $\lambda$, $\lambda_1\le s$ by the first-row bound, so $n\ge s+d\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ and the padded character polynomial lemma gives $\chi_{V(\lambda)_n}=P_\lambda$ of degree $\le|\lambda|$ on that range; additivity of characters gives $\chi_{V_n}=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda P_\lambda$, a character polynomial of weighted degree at most $d$ and with rational coefficients, as a function on all $S_n$ with $n\ge s+d$. Uniqueness: if two polynomials of weighted degree $\le d$ agree on $S_n$ for all $n\ge s+d$, then by the uniqueness statement of the character-polynomial definition they are equal.

items.title: Each padded irreducible family is realised by a finitely generated FI-module
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $\lambda$ be a partition with $|\lambda|=m$. There is an FI-module $V(\lambda)$ over $k$ with $$V(\lambda)_n\cong\begin{cases}V_{\lambda[n]},&n\ge m+\lambda_1,\ \varnothing,&n<m+\lambda_1.\end{cases}$$ It is finitely generated in degree $m+\lambda_1$, has $\operatorname{weight}(V(\lambda))=m$ and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(V(\lambda))=\lambda_1$.
items.strategy: Define $V(\lambda)_n\subseteq M(\lambda)_n$ as the span of the irreducible constituent $V_{\lambda[n]}$ for $n\ge d:=m+\lambda_1$ and put it equal to $0$ below $d$; the branching lemma (i) describes the constituents of $M(\lambda)_n$ as the shapes obtained from $\lambda$ by adding one box in each of $n-m$ different columns, and $\lambda[n]$ is exactly the resulting partition once $n-m\ge\lambda_1$, while every other constituent has strictly fewer than $m$ boxes below its first row. Any $S_m$-equivariant map $V(\lambda)_m\to M(\lambda)_n$ has image contained in $V(\lambda)_n$ because $V(\lambda)_m$ is the constituent with $m$ boxes below the first row and every other constituent of $M(\lambda)_n$ has fewer; applying this to the maps $f_*$ shows that the subspaces form a sub-FI-module. Injectivity of $f_*\colon M(\lambda)_d\to M(\lambda)_n$ shows $\operatorname{span}(V(\lambda)_d)_n\neq0$, and irreducibility of $V(\lambda)_n$ gives $\operatorname{span}(V(\lambda)_d)_n=V(\lambda)_n$, so $V(\lambda)$ is generated in degree $d$. The weight is $m$ because $\lambda[n]$ has $m$ boxes below the first row and every other constituent fewer; injectivity degree $0$ follows from containment in $M(\lambda)$ and the free-module bound; surjectivity degree $\lambda_1$ follows by writing $V(\lambda)$ as a quotient of $M(\lambda[d])=M(\lambda_1,\lambda_1,\dots)$ generated by $V(\lambda)_d\cong V_{\lambda[d]}$ and applying $\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(\mu))=\mu_1=\lambda_1$, with sharpness from the coinvariant lemma (ii) at $a=|\lambda|$, where $\Phi_mV(\lambda)_{\lambda_1}\cong V_\lambda\neq0$ while $\Phi_mV(\lambda)_{\lambda_1-1}=0$.

items.title: Dimensions of finitely generated FI-modules are eventually polynomial
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values, weight $d$ and stability degree $s$, with character polynomial $P_V$ as above. Then $$\dim_kV_n=P_V(n,0,0,\dots)$$ for every $n\ge s+d$; in particular $\dim_kV_n$ is given by a polynomial in $n$ of degree at most $d$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
items.strategy: Evaluate the character polynomial identity at the identity permutation: $\chi_{V_n}(\mathrm{id})=P_V(X_1(\mathrm{id}),X_2(\mathrm{id}),\dots)=P_V(n,0,0,\dots)$, because the identity has $n$ fixed points and no cycles of length $\ge2$, and $\dim_kV_n=\chi_{V_n}(\mathrm{id})$ for a finite-dimensional module.

items.title: The permutation FI-module has character polynomial $X_1$
items.statement: For every finite set $S$ let $V_S$ be the free $k$-module on $S$, and on an injection $f\colon S\to S'$ let $V(f)$ be the linear extension of $f$. This is the FI-module $M(1)$ ([[def-free-fi-module-generated-by-an-sm-module]]) with $V_n\cong k^n$ the permutation representation of $S_n$; it is generated by $V_{\{1\}}$. Its character is the character polynomial $X_1$ of weighted degree $1$ ([[def-character-polynomial-in-cycle-counts]]): for every $n$ and every $\sigma\in S_n$, $\chi_{V_n}(\sigma)=X_1(\sigma)$, the number of fixed points.
items.strategy: The transition maps are functorial by construction, so $V$ is an FI-module, and $M(1)$ has the stated basis of injections $1\to S$; the image of the generating element is all of $M(1)$ because every injection $1\to S$ is the image of the single injection $1\to\{1\}$ for some bijection of $S$. The matrix of $\sigma$ in that basis is a permutation matrix, so its trace is the number of $1\times1$ blocks, i.e. the number of fixed points, which is $X_1(\sigma)$; this holds for every $n$, matching the character-polynomial identity on the whole range.

items.title: The exterior square of the permutation FI-module has character polynomial $\binom{X_1}{2}-X_2$
items.statement: Let $V=M(1)$ be the permutation FI-module of the previous example and define $W_S:=\Lambda^2V_S$ with $W(f)=\Lambda^2V(f)$; this is an FI-module, and $W_n\cong\Lambda^2(k^n)$ as an $S_n$-module. Its character is the character polynomial $\binom{X_1}{2}-X_2$ of weighted degree $2$: for every $n$ and every $\sigma\in S_n$, $\chi_{W_n}(\sigma)=\binom{X_1(\sigma)}{2}-X_2(\sigma)$, where $X_1(\sigma)$ is the number of fixed points and $X_2(\sigma)$ the number of $2$-cycles.
items.strategy: Functoriality of $\Lambda^2$ makes $W$ an FI-module with the same transition-map compatibility. Fix $\sigma\in S_n$ and use the basis $x_i\wedge x_j$, $i<j$: the coefficient of $x_i\wedge x_j$ in $\sigma\cdot(x_i\wedge x_j)$ is nonzero exactly when $\sigma$ preserves the unordered pair $\{i,j\}$, and it equals $+1$ when both elements are fixed and $-1$ when they are exchanged by the $2$-cycle $(i\,j)$; a permutation that preserves a two-element set acts on it either as the identity or as its transposition, so there are no other diagonal entries. Hence the trace is $\binom{X_1(\sigma)}{2}-X_2(\sigma)$, which is a character polynomial of weighted degree $2$ ([[def-character-polynomial-in-cycle-counts]]), using that the character of $\Lambda^2$ is determined by the character of $V$ ([[thm-characters-of-direct-sums-tensor-products-and-duals]]).

items.title: The padded family $V((2,1))$ begins at rank five, with weight three and stability degree two
items.statement: Let $\lambda=(2,1)$, so $|\lambda|=3$ and $\lambda_1=2$. The first-row padding $\lambda[n]=(n-3,2,1)$ ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]) is a partition exactly for $n\ge5=3+2$: for $n=3$ the sequence $(0,2,1)$ is not weakly decreasing and $\lambda[3]$ is not a partition, for $n=4$ one gets $(1,2,1)$, still not a partition, and for $n\ge5$ it is. Accordingly the FI-module $V((2,1))$ of [[prop-fi-module-realizing-one-padded-irreducible-family]] has $$V((2,1))_n\cong\begin{cases}V_{(n-3,2,1)},&n\ge5,\ \varnothing,&n<5,\end{cases}$$ is generated in degree $5$, and has $\operatorname{weight}(V((2,1)))=3$ and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(V((2,1)))=2$.
items.strategy: Check the padding threshold from the definition: $\lambda[n]$ is a partition iff $n-|\lambda|\ge\lambda_1$, i.e. $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1=5$; for $n=3,4$ the first part is smaller than the second, and for $n\ge5$ the sequence is weakly decreasing. Then apply the realization proposition, which gives generation in degree $5$, weight $|\lambda|=3$ and stability degree $\lambda_1=2$; the two divergences from the padding threshold $n=|\lambda|=3$ are exactly the point of the example.

items.title: A pointwise one-dimensional FI-module that is not finitely generated
items.statement: Over a field $k$, define $V_S:=k\,e_S$ for every finite set $S$ (so $V$ is pointwise one-dimensional), let $V(f)\colon V_S\to V_{S'}$ send $e_S\mapsto e_{S'}$ when $f\colon S\to S'$ is a bijection, and $e_S\mapsto0$ when $f$ is not a bijection. Then $V$ is an FI-module with $\dim_kV_S=1$ for every $S$, but $V$ is not finitely generated: no finite set of elements generates it.
items.strategy: Functoriality: composites of bijections are bijections and give the identity on $k e_S$, and if $f\circ g$ is a bijection then both $f$ and $g$ are bijections; so if either of $f,g$ fails to be a bijection, the composite $V(f)V(g)$ and $V(f\circ g)$ are both $0$. Non-finite-generation: given finitely many generating elements, choose $M$ at least as large as the sizes of the finite sets on which they live; every generator lies in some $V_S$ with $|S|\le M$, and every injection from such an $S$ into a set $T$ with $|T|>M$ is a non-bijection, so its image is $0$; hence the generated sub-FI-module is contained in $\bigoplus_{|T|\le M}V_T$ and misses $e_T$ for $|T|=M+1$. The pointwise spaces are one-dimensional, so pointwise finite generation (even finite-dimensionality) does not imply finite generation.
